taxon.identityContext: The paper reports morphological identification and DNA analysis for collected specimens. This review does not independently re-identify specimens or adjudicate other name authorities.

sourceFacts.citation: Mutia, M.T.M. et al. (2025). The Philippine Journal of Fisheries 32(2):265-280. https://doi.org/10.31398/tpjf/32.2.2025A0001
sourceFacts.assessmentPeriod: The article analyzes NFRDI Taal Lake landed-catch assessment records from 2011 through 2022, gathered from 15 landing sites around the lake.
sourceFacts.reportedCatchExamples: The abstract reports 0.444 metric tons in 2011, 116.43 metric tons in 2014, 425.22 metric tons in 2018, and 479.99 metric tons in 2022; the table reports a 754.84 metric ton total for 2021.
sourceFacts.reportedGeographicSpread: The abstract says the fish expanded from three named municipalities in 2011 to all nine municipalities by 2015.
sourceFacts.tableConflict: Table 1 names eight landing municipalities, while the abstract says nine municipalities; the article text also distinguishes landing sites from municipalities. Do not infer a ninth municipality or treat missing rows as absence without resolving the source table and its underlying records.
sourceFacts.evidenceType: Secondary analysis of landed-catch assessment records. Landed catch is not a standardized lake-wide abundance estimate, an effort-corrected trend, or a current catch forecast.
sourceFacts.invasionLanguage: The article title and abstract describe the taxon as new, non-native and potentially invasive; do not convert the potential-risk wording into a verified regulatory or ecological classification.

accessAndRights.reviewMethod: Official NFRDI article page and PDF-indexed text reviewed; the journal copyright policy and DOAJ journal record were cross-checked. No local PDF or figure was retained.
accessAndRights.license: The journal policy states CC BY-NC 4.0 for submitted manuscripts; the reuse scope is noncommercial and requires attribution. Public-app and future-commercial-use fit has not been approved.
accessAndRights.excludedMaterial: No article prose, table, figure, catch totals, municipality rows, photographs or raw NFRDI assessment records are copied into the app.

nonClaims: The article is not a complete Taal Lake fish inventory and does not establish current abundance or catchability.
A landing-catch row does not prove absence from a municipality with no row, nor does it define where fish can be caught safely or legally.
The municipality count mismatch remains unresolved; no missing municipality is reconstructed from the map or abstract.
The article's noncommercial license does not authorize commercial use, and no project-wide legal review was performed.
nextAction: Seek a separately licensed or written-authorized Taal Lake stock-assessment table, resolve the eight-versus-nine municipality discrepancy against the underlying NFRDI records, and continue the broader CALABARZON inland fish baseline.
